newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Viasa's fate to be decided on Feb 8.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Viasa's fate to be decided on Feb 8.

text.p: The fate of troubled Venezuelan national airline Viasa will be finally decided at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on February 8, the company's executive board said.
It will be decided then "whether we increase the company's capital or declare it bankrupt," Victor Sanchez, executive secretary of the board, told reporters.

Viasa suspended all flights Thursday until the meeting. Sanchez, reading an official statement, said that decision had been taken "after analysing the risks of continuing operations under current circumstances".
Ten flights scheduled for Thursday were cancelled, including routes to Madrid and London, Buenos Aires, Lima, Bogota, Quito and Santo Domingo in Dominican Republic, pilots told Reuters.

Viasa, which suffered losses of $30 million last year, has been teetering on the brink of bankruptcy ever since workers rejected a restructuring plan proposed by Iberia Lineas Aereas de Espana SA a 45 percent shareholder, earlier this month.
The Venezuelan government, which holds 40 percent of the airline, has refused to pump more money into the airline.
